It is used in volume rendering to provide illustrative shading that enhances shape perception by mapping orientation to warm and cool tones [S1][S4, unofficial].

The claim states that the technique is used in volume rendering to provide illustrative shading that enhances shape perception by mapping orientation to warm and cool tones. Source [S1] explicitly states that the goal of 'Phong/Tone Shading' is to 'Convey shape by giving surfaces facing the light source “warm” colors, while other surfaces get “cooler” colors' and notes it is common in medical illustration. Source [S4] confirms that Tone Shading is a non-photorealistic rendering approach used in volume rendering (specifically mentioning 'In volume rendering, the gradient vector is used instead of the normal vector') and that its goal is to 'modify the tone of an object based on the orientation of that object relative to the light' using 'a warm color and a cool color' to maintain a 'spatial impression of the object' (shape perception). Both sources align perfectly with the claim.
